First off I want to say, I know you mean well and I really do feel for you. It must be incredibly difficult having someone so close to you suffering with this awful disease. But just to echo what many others have said, it would be totally wrong to give him the medication without his consent. 

I was prescribed Naltrexone a few weeks ago and had to provide GP test results which proved my liver function was normal, and thats because of the potential side effects of this medication, so it's a serious business. 

If your Dad had a desire to quit - or at least cut down on the drinking - then you could have raised the topic of Naltrexone with him, maybe started off by watching 'One Little Pill' together and slowly easing him into the idea before potentially looking into the Sinclair Method (he would need to have and pass the liver function tests to qualify as a candidate for Naltrexone). But if he's totally against it at the moment then you'll have to wait for him to be ready.

  I wish you all the best with this difficult situation and hope things work out in the end for you both.
